facts.text: TE: TTF rose to ~EUR47.5/MWh but headed for a weekly loss of >2% on reports of a draft 60-day US-Iran ceasefire and nuclear-talks framework awaiting Trump's approval; Vance: a deal is 'close' but 'not there yet'.

10Y closes 28 May (PAP/Bloomberg table, unstamped, 07:52): Bund 2.96%, OAT 3.57%, BTP 3.68%, Bonos 3.38%, gilt 4.81% -> OAT-Bund 61bp, BTP-Bund 72bp, Spain 42bp; Schatz 2.56%, gilt 2Y 4.24%; CZ10 4.84%, HU10 5.42%, PL10 5.77%; UST10 4.44%, UST2 4.02%, JGB10 2.65%.

Kashkari: too early to conclude that an immediate rate hike is needed after the April PCE data (Odaily); Schmid (12:31): the priority is returning inflation to 2%, 'not the time to let our guard down'.

France May flash CPI 2.4% y/y (2.5% expected; April 2.2%), highest since Feb 2024 on energy (+16.8%); HICP 2.8% (2.9% expected); Q1 GDP revised to -0.1% q/q (flat flash), the first contraction since Q2 2020 (INSEE via TE/PAP).
Czech Q1 GDP +0.2% q/q confirmed (Q4 +0.7%), domestic demand weaker (CZSO via TE).

29 May morning: Brent (expiring July contract) $92.52 (-1.3%), set for a weekly fall of 10.5% (largest since 6 April) and a May drop of ~19% (largest monthly fall since 2020); Axios: US-Iran deal on extending the ceasefire and easing Hormuz restrictions agreed by negotiators but not approved by Trump; Fars: Iranian forces fired missiles at unspecified targets on Thursday evening (PAP).

TE: May flash HICP rose in France (2.8%, below forecasts), Spain (3.6%, in line; CPI steady at 3.2%) and Italy (3.3%, above forecasts, an over two-year high); German import prices +5.3% y/y in April (energy +31%).
Germany May flash CPI 2.6% y/y (April 2.9%), slightly below forecasts; HICP 2.7% (2.8% expected); core up to 2.5%, services 3.1%, energy 6.6% (Destatis via TE/PAP).

Governor Bowman: if the Fed keeps its credibility it can look through energy shocks; too early to judge the war's effect on inflation, temporary price shocks can be overlooked for now (Odaily 14:57/15:22).
Chicago PMI jumped to 62.7 in May (49.2 in April), the highest in over four years (TE); April wholesale inventories +0.5% m/m (0.8% expected) (PAP).

TE: UST10 ~4.45%, near three-week lows but up ~7bp in May; DXY ~99, near two-week lows, ~+1% in May (16:16); Bund 10Y down to 2.93%, the lowest since April (17:10); gilt 10Y ~4.8%, near April lows, -19bp in May.

Trump (Truth Social, ~16:54): convening a Situation Room meeting for a 'final decision' on Iran; Iran must never have nuclear weapons, Hormuz must open immediately, the naval blockade would be lifted and enriched uranium removed and destroyed with Iran and the IAEA (Odaily 16:54-17:04; PAP 18:04); Fars sources denied his account (17:49).

PAP digest: a Russian drone hit a 10-storey apartment block in Galati, south-eastern Romania; NATO and the Commission condemned it and von der Leyen said a 21st sanctions package is being prepared; Hungary's PM Magyar assured Rutte that Budapest will again be a reliable ally.

ECB's Simkus: after the widely expected June hike a second move is 'more likely than not' - July, September or October; Radev: the cost of waiting may exceed the cost of acting early (PAP European close).

29 May European close: UST10 4.44% (-1bp), Bund 10Y 2.94% (-2bp); Brent July $92 (-1.8%), WTI $87.6; EUR/USD 1.169; USD/JPY 159.2; Stoxx600 +2.4% in May (PAP; its 'DXY 99.8' conflicts with TE ~99, not used).

Senior US officials: Trump's two-hour Situation Room meeting ended without a decision; unfreezing Iranian funds still under discussion (Odaily); CENTCOM (20:41) warned it will act near Hormuz and strike vessels supporting the blockade breach.
Wall Street closed at record highs (Dow 51,032, S&P 500 7,580); May: Nasdaq +8%, S&P +5%, a ninth straight weekly gain; Brent July $91.99 (-1.8%) as the contract expired (PAP 22:27).

Bloomberg (via Odaily): an Iranian ballistic-missile attack on an air base in Kuwait lightly injured several Americans and damaged two MQ-9 drones; the US said its blockade of Iranian ports remains in force (13:07).

Rezaei (adviser to Iran's supreme leader): Trump is 'betraying diplomacy for the third time' with excessive demands; Iranian MPs to approve a plan for 'sovereign jurisdiction' over Hormuz (14:15) (Odaily).

NYT (via Odaily): Trump tightened the terms of the framework deal and sent amendments to Tehran; Axios (03:30): revisions concern nuclear material and Hormuz; Trump (Fox, 03:13): a deal is 'very close', military action if it is unfair to the US.

PAP weekend digest: Ghalibaf (Sun): no deal ending the war until Iranian rights are guaranteed; Tasnim: exchanges on the draft MoU continue, nothing finalised; Malta's Labour won the 30 May snap election.

CENTCOM: weekend 'self-defence' strikes on Iranian radars and drone command posts in southern Iran; two Iranian ballistic missiles aimed at a US base in Kuwait were shot down; the IRGC said it hit a US air base (Odaily 05:28-05:38; PAP).

10Y closes 29 May (PAP/Bloomberg table): Bund 2.94%, OAT 3.55%, BTP 3.65%, Bonos 3.35%, gilt 4.81% -> OAT-Bund 61bp, BTP-Bund 71bp, Spain 41bp; Schatz 2.53%, gilt 2Y 4.21%; CZ10 4.78%, HU10 5.30%, PL10 5.64%. Live 06:30: UST10 4.47%, UST2 4.03%, JGB10 2.69%.

PAP week ahead: euro-area May HICP expected at ~3.2% (3.0% in April); markets price ~70bp of ECB hikes to H1 2027, a June hike seen as near-certain (Schnabel: hike in June even with a US-Iran deal); US payrolls seen +96k (115k in April) with unemployment 4.3%, the last report before the first FOMC chaired by Warsh (16-17 June).
1 Jun morning: Brent (now the August contract) $93.25 (+2.3%), rebounding from a six-week low as the US and Iran traded amendments to the draft deal over the weekend with no clear progress (PAP).

May final manufacturing PMIs: euro area 51.6 (flash 51.4; April 52.2), Germany 50.1, France 49.7; UK 53.9, the strongest in four years; euro-area unemployment 6.3% in April (6.2% expected) (S&P Global/Eurostat via TE/PAP).

Tasnim: Iran's negotiators will halt talks and the exchange of texts via mediators over Israel's strikes in Lebanon and move to 'fully close' Hormuz; Brent jumped >5% to ~$96 (TE 15:43; Odaily 15:13).
TE: UST10 rose to 4.51%; odds of a December Fed hike above 60% (15:48; >50% at 15:55); traders see a 50% chance of a hike as early as October (Odaily 15:54).
ISM manufacturing 54.0 in May (53.0-53.3 expected; April 52.7), the strongest since May 2022; S&P Global US manufacturing PMI 55.1 (final); construction spending above forecasts (ISM/S&P via TE/PAP).
TE: Bund 10Y back above 3%; markets now expect at least two ECB hikes this year with >90% probability of the first on 11 June.
TE: gilt 10Y back above 4.9%; almost two BoE hikes priced for 2026, the first fully priced for September.

PAP digest: Hungary's PM Magyar told President Sulyok the government will take legal steps if he does not resign after his deadline expired at midnight; EU gas storage 40.1% full vs a 54.1% five-year average (GIE).
Sources: OPEC+ to raise output by ~188k b/d in July (Odaily).

1 Jun European close: UST10 4.50% (+5bp), Bund 10Y 3.00% (+7bp); Brent $96.79 (+6.2%; PAP still labels it July), WTI $93.60 (+7.1%); TTF EUR49.03/MWh (+6.3%); gold $4,504 (-1.9%); EUR/USD 1.1622, USD/JPY 159.67 (PAP).

Trump: he does not mind a pause in talks ('silence would be very good'), oil prices will fall soon; he said Israel and Hezbollah agreed to stop attacking each other and Iran talks continue; Brent pared gains to ~$95 (PAP 21:02; Odaily 21:29; TE 22:21).
Wall Street: S&P 500 and Nasdaq at record closes on AI optimism despite the Iran headlines; Brent $95.28 (+4.6%) (PAP 22:16).
TE: markets price ~78% probability of a BoJ hike at its June meeting; the yen's weakness drew a fresh verbal warning from Tokyo (04:20).

US media: US-Iran talks back on track (Odaily 05:26); an Iranian source: the final text is still under discussion (08:23); Trump (ABC, Mon): a deal to extend the truce and reopen Hormuz possible within a week.

10Y closes 1 Jun (PAP/Bloomberg table): Bund 3.00%, OAT 3.63%, BTP 3.74%, Bonos 3.43%, gilt 4.90% -> OAT-Bund 63bp, BTP-Bund 74bp, Spain 43bp; Schatz 2.63%, gilt 2Y 4.33%; CZ10 4.83%, HU10 5.36%, PL10 5.72%. Live 06:40: UST10 4.44%, UST2 4.03%, JGB10 2.62%.
Hungary Q1 GDP growth confirmed at 1.7% y/y (KSH via TE).
TE: gilt 10Y down to 4.85%; nearly two BoE hikes priced this year, the first fully priced for September.
TE: Bund yields fell with oil; money markets price a 95% probability of a 25bp ECB hike next week.
Euro-area May flash HICP 3.2% y/y (3.2% expected; April 3.0%), the highest since Sep 2023; core 2.5% (2.4% expected; April 2.2%); services 3.5%, energy 10.9% (Eurostat).
Hammack: the Fed may need to act quickly to address high inflation (Odaily).
JOLTS: job openings rose by 731k to 7.618m in April (6.88m expected), the highest since Nov 2024; quits fell (BLS via TE/PAP).

Rubio: an Iran deal could come 'today, tomorrow or next week'; no sanctions relief just for reopening Hormuz, nuclear talks could take months (Odaily 16:32-16:51; PAP); Fars: message exchanges with the US paused for several days; an Iranian joint-command deputy said renewed war with the US is inevitable (PAP).

PAP digest (tariffs): the White House said Trump temporarily cut tariffs on some steel, aluminium and copper products (farm machinery, HVAC from 25% to 15%); the EP trade committee (INTA) backed implementing the EU-US tariff commitments.
2 Jun European close: UST10 4.45% (-1bp), Bund 10Y 2.97% (-3bp); Brent Aug $94.87 (-0.2%); TTF EUR47.56/MWh (-3.1%); gold $4,531; EUR/USD 1.1640, USD/JPY 159.88 (PAP).

Trump: talks with Iran continue 'but nobody knows where they lead'; time for Tehran to make a deal (PAP 21:02); TE (22:34): WTI back above $93 as Iran reviews a US proposal without contact for days; Wall Street at new records.

IRGC: after a US shell hit an Iranian tanker near Hormuz and a US strike on Qeshm, it fired missiles at a US/Israeli vessel and missiles and drones at a US air base and the Fifth Fleet HQ (Odaily 02:10); CENTCOM: intercepted Iranian missiles and drones and hit Qeshm Island in 'self-defence'; Iranian drones and missiles hit Kuwait's international airport on Wednesday, one killed (PAP digest).
ECB's Wunsch: a US-Iran peace deal before next week's meeting would not weaken the case for a hike (Odaily).

10Y closes 2 Jun (PAP/Bloomberg table): Bund 2.98%, OAT 3.60%, BTP 3.69%, Bonos 3.39%, gilt 4.86% -> OAT-Bund 62bp, BTP-Bund 71bp, Spain 41bp; Schatz 2.62%, gilt 2Y 4.31%; CZ10 4.81%, HU10 5.35%, PL10 5.68%. Live 06:32: UST10 4.46%, UST2 4.06%, JGB10 2.62%.
May final services PMI: euro area 47.7 (flash 46.4), composite 48.5 (flash 47.5); Germany services 48.1, France 44.3; UK services 49.3 (flash 47.9) (S&P Global via PAP).

Trump: Iran agreed not to have nuclear weapons and its supreme leader is involved in the talks; open to meeting him; the naval blockade could last until Labor Day (7 Sep) but he expects a deal soon (Odaily 12:08-12:34).
ADP private payrolls +122k in May (117k expected; April revised to 105k), the most since Jan 2025 (ADP via TE/PAP).
TE: Treasury yields rose further after ADP; markets price an 85% probability of a 25bp Fed hike by year-end, up from 60% a week ago.
TE: the ECB is expected to hike next week, with traders also pricing another 25bp in September.
ISM services 54.5 in May (53.8 expected; April 53.6), prices paid 71.3, the highest since Aug 2022, employment 47.9; April factory orders +4.8%, durables +8.0% (final) (ISM/Census via TE/PAP).

PAP digest (tariffs): Bloomberg: the US plans new tariffs of at least 10% on imports from 60 countries, rebuilding the tariff wall after the Supreme Court struck down earlier duties; the Commission will treat energy-related state spending leniently under EU fiscal rules.

3 Jun European close: UST10 4.50% (+5bp), UST30 5.00%, Bund 10Y 3.04% (+6bp); Brent Aug $97.92 (+2.0%), WTI $95.89; DXY 99.44, EUR/USD 1.1605, USD/JPY 159.99 (PAP; its TTF and gold lines repeat earlier prints and are not used).
Wall Street fell as oil and Treasury yields rose (UST10 near 4.5%); per CME FedWatch the Fed will raise rates by at least 25bp by year-end; Brent $98.06 (+2.2%) (PAP 22:22).

Logan: the Fed may need to raise rates later this year to bring inflation back to 2%; Beige Book: prices rose at a moderate to strong pace in most districts, Middle East energy costs the main driver (Odaily 22:59/23:05).
TE: DXY near a two-month high; markets assign an 85% probability to a 25bp Fed hike by year-end.

BoJ's Ueda: the bank should weigh the costs and benefits of a hike if inflation risks begin to outweigh downside growth risks (TE); PAP: he suggested a high probability of a June hike if upside inflation risks prove larger (08:17).

10Y closes 3 Jun (PAP/Bloomberg table): Bund 3.04%, OAT 3.67%, BTP 3.78%, Bonos 3.46%, gilt 4.93% -> OAT-Bund 63bp, BTP-Bund 74bp, Spain 42bp; Schatz 2.67%, gilt 2Y 4.37%; CZ10 4.83%, HU10 5.47%, PL10 5.70%. Live 06:28: UST10 4.48%, UST2 4.07%, JGB10 2.67%.
TE: markets price a near-certain 25bp ECB hike on 11 June, with two or possibly three increases this year.
Czech May flash CPI 2.1% y/y (2.3% expected; April 2.5%), +0.1% m/m; food -1.9% y/y (CZSO via TE).
Euro-area April retail sales -0.4% m/m (-0.3% expected; March revised to +0.8%), +1.0% y/y (Eurostat via PAP).
TE: nearly two BoE hikes priced this year, the first expected in September; investors pared BoE bets later as oil fell (17:46).
Initial jobless claims 225k (212-214k expected), the highest since early February; continuing claims 1.777m; Q1 productivity revised lower (DoL/BLS via TE/PAP).
Fitch raised its 2026 Brent forecast to $87/bbl after 14 weeks of Hormuz closure (Odaily); Bessent: the Iran conflict has been 'paused' (17:06).

PAP (4 Jun, Polish holiday): Netanyahu: Israel and the US are ready to strike Iran again if needed; a US-brokered Israel-Lebanon ceasefire was announced but Hezbollah rejected it (AFP); Brent Aug $95.16 (-2.7%) after 16:00.
PAP holiday digest: an IAEA report asks Iran to say urgently what happened to its ~440kg of enriched uranium; Czech PM Babis wants Merz to negotiate for the EU on Ukraine.
Wall Street: Dow +1.7% to 51,562 as investors rotated out of chips after Broadcom; Brent $95.32 (-2.6%), WTI $93.23 (PAP 22:11).

10Y closes 4 Jun (PAP/Bloomberg table in ticker layout, 05:55, unstamped): Bund 3.02%, OAT 3.67%, BTP 3.77%, Bonos 3.45%, gilt 4.90% -> OAT-Bund 65bp, BTP-Bund 75bp, Spain 43bp; Schatz 2.66%, gilt 2Y 4.33%; CZ10 4.79%, HU10 5.50%; UST10 4.47%, UST2 4.05%, JGB10 2.67%.
RBI held the repo rate at 5.25% (neutral stance) and cut its FY2026/27 GDP forecast to 6.6% (TE).
Romania Q1 GDP -1.2% y/y (second estimate; flash -1.7%), the first contraction since Q4 2020 (INS via TE).
Euro-area Q1 GDP revised to -0.2% q/q (+0.1% before) and +0.3% y/y, dragged by Ireland (-12.1% q/q); employment +0.1% (Eurostat).

Market report: Iran told Pakistan it accepts moving part of its uranium to a third country (Odaily 11:16), denied by a Fars source (14:17: nuclear issues not yet discussed); Iranian navy fired warning shots at a US destroyer in the Gulf of Oman (13:43).
CME FedWatch before payrolls: June hold 96.4%; July hold 88.5%, hike 8.2% (Odaily).
Payrolls +172k in May (85k expected), April revised up to +179k (two-month revision +93k); unemployment 4.3%, participation 61.8%; average hourly earnings +0.3% m/m (BLS via TE/PAP).
Rate futures: December Fed-hike probability rose from 48% to 63% after payrolls (Jin10 via Odaily); TE: a 25bp hike by year-end now almost fully priced, UST10 +5-6bp to 4.53-4.54%.
TE: gilt 10Y back above 4.9% on US yields and politics: Greater Manchester mayor Andy Burnham announced he will challenge Keir Starmer for the Labour leadership.
PAP digest: a sea drone of unknown origin exploded near Romania's Constanta port (no casualties); von der Leyen and Costa expressed solidarity with Romania.
Hammack: with the labour market roughly in balance, a near-term rate hike may be appropriate (Odaily).
Reuters poll: the ECB will raise the deposit rate to 2.25% on 11 June, another hike possible in September; May core HICP 2.5% (PAP European close).
5 Jun European close: EUR/USD -0.7% to 1.1532, USD/JPY 160.3; Brent ~$93.4 (-1.7%), WTI ~$90.7 at 18:00; UST10 above 4.5%, UST30 above 5% (PAP).
Wall Street fell sharply, the Nasdaq the most in over a year, as yields jumped (UST10 >4.5%, UST30 >5%) and bitcoin dropped below $60k; Brent $93.01 (-2.1%) (PAP 22:16).
IRGC: missile strikes on US bases in response to US actions on Sirik and Qeshm (Odaily 03:56); CENTCOM denied damage at the Fifth Fleet HQ (04:19).

Fars: Iran will charge $150k-2m per tanker crossing Hormuz, partly payable in goods (Odaily 12:14); Trump (NBC): no unfreezing of assets or sanctions relief in advance, Lebanon not required in a short-term deal, the sides are 'very close' (15:13); the Fed has no reason to raise rates (15:18).

PAP weekend digest: OPEC+ will raise output by 188k b/d from July; Israel struck Hezbollah targets in Beirut's southern suburbs on Sunday and Iran threatened a 'decisive and painful response'; Iran accused the US of violating the truce by striking coastal radars at Goruk and Qeshm; CENTCOM downed two Iranian drones over Hormuz.

Iran fired missiles at Israel for the first time since the 8 April ceasefire; WTI +3% in early Asian trade (Odaily 00:19); the Israeli air force struck military targets in western and central Iran (03:29).
TE: after payrolls markets price ~70% for a December Fed hike (from ~50% before the report); the dollar near multi-month highs.
TE: TTF surged >5% to ~EUR51/MWh, a near three-week high, as Iran and Israel exchanged strikes.

PAP week ahead: a June ECB hike to a 2.25% deposit rate is seen as a done deal; >60% of Reuters-polled economists expect one more this year, probably in September; BoC (2.25%) and CBRT (37%) seen on hold; Wells Fargo sees US May CPI at 4.2%.

10Y closes 5 Jun (PAP/Bloomberg table): Bund 3.04%, OAT 3.69%, BTP 3.80%, Bonos 3.48%, gilt 4.90% -> OAT-Bund 65bp, BTP-Bund 76bp, Spain 44bp; Schatz 2.69%, gilt 2Y 4.34%; CZ10 4.88%, HU10 5.44%, PL10 5.79%. Live 06:31: UST10 4.57%, UST2 4.19%, JGB10 2.72%.
German April factory orders -3.8% m/m (-1.2% expected; March revised to +4.5%) (Destatis via TE/PAP).
8 Jun morning: Brent +4.8% to $97.6; all Asian indices down as AI trades unwound and Fed-hike bets grew (PAP).
TE: two BoE hikes fully priced this year; gilt 10Y near the May peak; MPC's Taylor: rates are 'quite restrictive', no need for further increases.
TE: money markets price the ECB deposit rate at ~2.7% by December, a near-certain June hike and a second in September (three hikes priced, 09:56).

Trump: Israel and Iran must stop firing immediately (Odaily 11:40); Iran announced the end of its operations against Israel (13:19) and Israel paused strikes at Trump's request (14:25); Iran's envoy in Moscow: Hormuz will open on terms set by Iran and Oman, including transit fees (Reuters via PAP).
TE: markets assign 70% to a December Fed hike, up from 45% a week earlier (CME FedWatch); ~52% for a hike as soon as October (14:16).

PAP digest: Kallas: Hungary lifted its veto on EUR6.6bn of European Peace Facility reimbursements; Hungary's integrity authority wants Orban-era officials investigated over EU funds; euro-area Sentix -13.4 (-14.0 expected); EU gas storage 42.1% vs 56.5% average.
8 Jun European close: UST10 4.55% (+2bp), Bund 10Y 3.06% (+2bp); Brent Aug $94.58 (+1.6%), WTI $91.57; TTF EUR49.99/MWh (+3.1%); gold $4,363; EUR/USD 1.1543, USD/JPY 160.11 (PAP).
CENTCOM disabled an empty tanker bound for Iran, the seventh ship hit for breaching the blockade (PAP 21:02).

10Y closes 8 Jun (PAP/Bloomberg table): Bund 3.06%, OAT 3.84%, BTP 3.83%, Bonos 3.50%, gilt 4.94% -> OAT-Bund 78bp (FR10 +15bp, FR5 +16bp on the day with no French news found - flagged), BTP-Bund 77bp, Spain 44bp; Schatz 2.71%, gilt 2Y 4.38%; CZ10 4.91%, HU10 5.52%, PL10 5.85%. Live 06:28: UST10 4.56%, UST2 4.16%, JGB10 2.71%.

Trump: the blockade is raising pressure and the US is 'very close' to a very good deal (Odaily 07:41); talks in the 'final stretch', a verdict within a day or two (10:40); AP: a big chance of signing within two to three days (PAP).
German April industrial output +0.4% m/m (in line), exports +0.9% (-0.5% expected) (Destatis via PAP).
Hungary May CPI 1.8% y/y (2.3% expected; April 2.1%); food 0.5%, household energy -2%, services 4.3% (KSH via TE).
TE: at least a 25bp BoE hike priced for September, with a strong likelihood of a second; gilts steady as Middle East tensions eased.
Erste: CEE8 GDP growth seen at 2.3% in 2026 (2.7% before the war); Romania expected in recession this year; Hungary's forecast raised to 1.7% (PAP).
TE: probability of a Fed hike as early as October ~51%; ~70% for December (17:13); NFIB small-business optimism 95.3, the lowest since Oct 2024 (PAP).

9 Jun European close: UST10 4.54% (-2bp), Bund 10Y 3.05% (-1bp); Brent Aug $90.88 (PAP prints '+3.57%' - a sign error, the price fell ~4%), WTI $89.61; TTF EUR48.74 (-2.2%); gold $4,298 (-1.5%), silver $65.5 (-4.4%); EUR/USD 1.1553 (PAP).
Trump: Iran shot down a US Apache helicopter over Hormuz on Monday evening (both pilots safe) and the US must respond (PAP).
US Energy Secretary Wright: tanker traffic through Hormuz rising 'very significantly', but normal flows will take months after any deal (PAP 21:06).
Gold closed at $4,286.4 (-~2%), the lowest close since 10 Dec 2025 and -18% since the war began; silver $65.24; S&P 500 and Nasdaq fell; Brent $91.87 (-2.5%) (PAP 22:13).

US officials: a second round of US strikes on Iranian air defences and radars underway (Odaily 01:30); CENTCOM (03:01): strikes on air-defence, ground-control and radar sites near Hormuz completed as a 'proportional' response to the Apache downing; Iran hit a US base in Jordan (03:58) and the IRGC sent drones at the Fifth Fleet in Bahrain.

10Y closes 9 Jun (PAP/Bloomberg table): Bund 3.04%, OAT 3.81%, BTP 3.80%, Bonos 3.48%, gilt 4.90% -> OAT-Bund 77bp, BTP-Bund 76bp, Spain 44bp; Schatz 2.67%, gilt 2Y 4.33%; CZ10 4.88%, HU10 5.43%, PL10 5.72%. Live 06:32: UST10 4.54%, UST2 4.14%, JGB10 2.70%.
10 Jun morning: Brent Aug $91.46 (flat) after the latest US-Iran strikes; analysts warn of a prolonged near-total Hormuz closure (PAP).
Czech May CPI confirmed at 2.1% y/y (CZSO via TE).
Trump: Iran took too long to negotiate and 'will have to pay the price' (Odaily 13:05); Iran was hit hard yesterday and will be struck again today (17:53).
TE: Bund 10Y approached 3.1% as inflation worries and ECB hike expectations intensified ahead of Thursday.
CME FedWatch before CPI: June hold 98.2%; July hike 12.6% (Odaily); Jin10: ~70% for a hike by end-2026 priced before the data (14:47).
US May CPI 4.2% y/y (in line; April 3.8%), the highest since April 2023, +0.5% m/m; core 2.9% y/y (in line), +0.2% m/m (0.3% expected); energy +23.5%, gasoline +40.5% (BLS via TE/PAP).
CME FedWatch after CPI: June hold 96.3%; July hike 10.3% (Odaily); TE: hike bets trimmed slightly, but a December quarter-point hike remains fully priced.
Bank of Canada held at 2.25% for a fifth meeting, looking through the war's near-term inflation impact but ready to raise if needed (TE).

10 Jun European close: UST10 4.53% (+1bp), Bund 10Y 3.08% (+4bp); Brent Aug $92.83 (+1.5%), WTI $89.81; DXY 99.89, EUR/USD 1.1544, USD/JPY 160.52 (PAP; its TTF and gold lines are stale/inconsistent and not used); gold had erased its 2026 gains, below $4,200 (Odaily 12:11).
Trump (White House briefing): the US will strike Iran 'very hard' again, still on Wednesday; more than 200 merchant ships crossed Hormuz with US help, >100m barrels reached the market (PAP 21:02).
Wall Street fell sharply (chipmakers led) after Trump said talks were taking too long and threatened more strikes; Brent $93.45 (+2.2%) (PAP 22:08).

CENTCOM completed the latest strikes in southern Iran (air defences, radars, drone command) (Odaily 03:08); the IRGC fired drones and missiles at US bases in Kuwait, Bahrain and Jordan; Reuters: despite the fire, the sides still exchange MoU details on a frozen-funds mechanism (PAP).
TE: TTF rose to EUR50.3/MWh, the highest in over three weeks, as Iran closed Hormuz to all shipping after a second day of US strikes.
TE: UST10 steady; traders slightly scaled back Fed-hike bets after CPI, but a December quarter-point hike remains fully priced.

10Y closes 10 Jun (PAP/Bloomberg table): Bund 3.08%, OAT 3.85%, BTP 3.85%, Bonos 3.52%, gilt 4.93% -> OAT-Bund 77bp, BTP-Bund 77bp, Spain 44bp; Schatz 2.72%, gilt 2Y 4.37%; CZ10 4.89%, HU10 5.48%, PL10 5.72%. Live 06:29: UST10 4.55%, UST2 4.13%, JGB10 2.68%.
Before the decision: traders fully price a 25bp ECB hike today and up to three hikes this year (PAP 09:29); Jefferies: the ECB may hike only once (Odaily 08:34).
TE: at least a 25bp BoE hike priced for September and a probability of a second by year-end; gilt 10Y 4.94%, near the highest since 21 May.
CBRT held the one-week repo rate at 37% for a third meeting, as expected; the energy shock lifted the underlying inflation trend (TE).

ECB raised its three key rates by 25bp - DFR 2.25%, MRO 2.40%, MLF 2.65%, effective 17 June - its first hike since 2023 after six holds: the Middle East war generates inflationary pressure and a hike is justified across scenarios; Bund 10Y -3bp to 3.05% after the decision; next meeting 22-23 July (PAP 14:25).
US May PPI +1.1% m/m (0.7% expected), 6.5% y/y; core below expectations; initial claims 229k (220k expected) (BLS/DoL via TE/PAP).
Trump: the US will strike Iran 'VERY HARD' tonight and will soon seize Kharg Island and other oil infrastructure, taking control of its oil and gas markets 'as with Venezuela'; Brent $93.40 (PAP).
World Bank cut its 2026 global growth forecast to 2.5% (2.6% in January), assuming an average Brent of $94/bbl with the worst disruptions easing in July; downside scenario 1.3% growth (PAP).

ECB June projections: HICP 3.0% (2026), 2.3% (2027), 2.0% (2028) vs 2.6/2.0/2.1 in March; core 2.5% in 2026-27; GDP 0.8/1.2/1.5% (0.9/1.3/1.4); oil assumption $96.9/bbl for 2026; severe scenario HICP 4.0% (2026) and 5.3% (2027) (PAP 16:17; TE).

Lagarde: the hike was unanimous; decisions meeting by meeting and data-dependent; risks to growth tilted to the downside, to inflation to the upside; inflation back at target in H2 2027 (PAP digest, 14:45 press conference).
PAP digest: UK Defence Secretary John Healey resigned, citing a lack of money for defence; the IAEA board adopted a US-backed resolution demanding Iran declare its enriched uranium.

After the decision investors trimmed further-hike bets slightly: the next move priced for September, some pricing a third; a July move not excluded (bank comment via PAP); Denmark's central bank hiked 25bp to 1.85% in tandem (TE 17:16).

Trump cancelled the strikes planned for tonight (Odaily 19:31); the blockade stays until an agreement, whose signing time and place will be announced soon (19:32); 'a great war settlement' reached, a final deal possible within days (21:33); Iranian media: no text approved yet (20:34).
Wall Street rallied (Dow +1.9%, S&P 500 +1.75%, Nasdaq +2.5%) on Trump's deal comments; Brent Aug $88.63 (-4.8%), WTI $85.94 (PAP 22:48).

Trump: the MoU requires the immediate reopening of Hormuz without tolls, with gradual sanctions relief tied to Iranian compliance and a 60-day ceasefire extension including Lebanon (Odaily 05:37); Fars: Iran has not yet approved but probably will (PAP).

10Y closes 11 Jun (PAP/Bloomberg table): Bund 3.03%, OAT 3.80%, BTP 3.80%, Bonos 3.47%, gilt 4.91% -> OAT-Bund 77bp, BTP-Bund 77bp, Spain 44bp; Schatz 2.68%, gilt 2Y 4.34%; CZ10 4.84%, HU10 5.41%, PL10 5.68%. Live 06:29: UST10 4.47%, UST2 4.07%, JGB10 2.65%.
UK April GDP -0.1% m/m (in line; March +0.3%), the first fall since August; industrial output flat (ONS via TE/PAP).
Germany May CPI confirmed at 2.6% y/y (Destatis via TE); France May CPI final 2.4% (INSEE, 08:45, PAP).
Romania May CPI 10.9% y/y (April 10.7%), the highest since April 2023; fuels +19.2%, services 13.5% (INS via TE).
TE: Bund 10Y fell below 3%, the lowest since 3 June, on Trump's deal remarks.
TE: gilt 10Y tumbled below 4.8%, the lowest since mid-April; April GDP casts doubt on further BoE tightening; focus on the 18 June Makerfield by-election with Burnham, a potential Starmer successor.
TE: money markets price another ECB hike, most likely in September, July a possibility.

G7 official: the MoU could be signed as early as Sunday in Geneva (Odaily 11:22); IRNA published a seven-point framework giving the US no role in Hormuz and no Iranian commitment to hand over its management (12:38-12:54).

Trump: Iran is acting dishonestly; terms leaked by Iran 'have nothing to do' with the written agreement (Odaily 15:42); Pakistan's PM: the final consensus text has been reached (18:30); a senior US official: the text is agreed, Iran gets economic benefits as it implements commitments including dismantling its nuclear programme and shipping out enriched uranium (PAP 21:06).
UMich sentiment rebounded to 48.9 in early June (46 expected; May 44.8, a record low); one-year inflation expectations eased (TE).
TE: UST10 rebounded to 4.5%, trimming Thursday's 10bp drop on new uncertainty over the Iran deal; Fed-hike bets were consolidated by the May CPI and PPI.
NYT (via PAP): the US will sharply cut the fighters and ships it makes available for NATO operations in Europe; the Commission proposed EUR540m of support for farmers hit by fertiliser costs.
12 Jun European close: Brent Aug $86.90 (-2.9%), WTI $84.38; EUR/USD 1.1571, USD/JPY 160.25; SpaceX priced its IPO at $135 (raising $75bn) and opened at $150, valued just under $2trn (PAP).
TE: Brent -3.4% to $87.3, about -6% on the week but >20% above its pre-war level; a US official put the chance of a deal being signed soon at 80%.

Pakistan's PM: the US-Iran agreement should be finalised within 24 hours, with electronic signing (Odaily 13:29); a senior US official: 'we believe we have reached an agreement' (16:35); Iran's MFA: any understanding is only for continued dialogue, not a final deal, and must include unfreezing assets (16:48); Pakistan's MFA: e-signing set for the 14th (17:52).
Trump: the US and Iran will sign on the 14th and Hormuz will reopen immediately after; Iran's MFA denied it (Odaily 01:46).

An Israeli strike on Beirut's southern suburbs: Ghalibaf said it makes continued dialogue 'impossible' (Odaily 14:47); Trump: the strike 'should not have happened' on a day the US was close to a deal (16:49).

PAP weekend digest: a senior Iranian official (Reuters): the final MoU provides for opening Hormuz and lifting US sanctions, timing unclear; Romania's President Dan named Adrian Vestea (PNL) prime minister after Eugen Tomac gave up the mandate; Putin called Trump on Ukraine and Iran.

Late Sunday (23:58, one minute before the info cut-off): Trump said a deal with Iran has been reached, authorising free passage through Hormuz and the immediate lifting of the US naval blockade; Pakistan's PM: an immediate and permanent cessation of military operations on all fronts including Lebanon, formal signing on Friday 19 June in Switzerland (Odaily).

digest.2026-06-01: 29-31 May: the negotiated 60-day US-Iran MoU still awaited Trump - his Situation Room meeting ended without a decision and he sent tougher terms back to Tehran; Iran hit a US base in Kuwait. Brent fell ~10% on the week (-19% in May) to ~$92; Bund 10Y 2.94% (7-week low), UST10 4.44%, gilt 4.81%. German May CPI 2.6%, French 2.4%; Simkus: a second ECB hike likely; ~46% for a December Fed hike.
digest.2026-06-02: 1 Jun: after weekend US-Iran exchanges of fire, Iran halted talks via mediators over Israel's strikes in Lebanon and threatened to fully close Hormuz; Brent (Aug) jumped up to 7% to ~$96-97, TTF +6% to EUR49; UST10 4.50%, Bund 10Y 3.00% (+7bp). >90% priced for a June ECB hike, ~two BoE hikes, >60% for a December Fed hike; ISM manufacturing 54.0. Trump later said Israel and Hezbollah agreed to halt attacks.
digest.2026-06-03: 2 Jun: euro-area May flash HICP 3.2% (core 2.5%, above forecasts) cemented a June ECB hike (95% priced); US JOLTS openings 7.6m; Rubio: an Iran deal possible within days, but no sanctions relief just for Hormuz; Trump cut some metal tariffs. Brent (Aug) ~$95, TTF EUR47.6; Bund 10Y 2.97%, UST10 4.45%; a June BoJ hike ~78% priced; Hungary Q1 GDP 1.7%.
digest.2026-06-05: 3-4 Jun: new US-Iran clashes (US strikes on Qeshm, an Iranian strike on Kuwait airport) while Trump said Iran agreed to forgo nuclear weapons; Brent ~$98, then ~$95. ADP 122k, ISM services 54.5 (prices 71.3) and Logan lifted odds of a 2026 Fed hike to ~85%; UST10 4.50%, Bund 10Y 3.04%; June ECB hike near-certain, 2-3 in 2026; Czech May CPI 2.1%; the US plans new tariffs of >=10% on 60 countries.
digest.2026-06-08: 5-7 Jun: payrolls +172k (85k expected) made a 25bp Fed hike by year-end almost fully priced (December 63%); UST10 >4.5%, Nasdaq's worst day in a year, EUR/USD 1.153; euro-area Q1 GDP revised to -0.2% q/q; Reuters poll: ECB to 2.25% on 11 June. Weekend: IRGC strikes on US bases, US strikes on Iranian radars, Israel hit Beirut; Iran plans Hormuz fees; OPEC+ +188k b/d; Burnham to challenge Starmer.
digest.2026-06-09: 8 Jun: Iran and Israel exchanged missile strikes for the first time since April before Trump got both to stop; Brent spiked ~5% to ~$97.6, then closed at ~$94.6; TTF ~EUR50. ~70% priced for a December Fed hike; ECB deposit rate ~2.7% by December; two BoE hikes priced. German April orders -3.8%; UST10 4.55%, Bund 10Y 3.06%; Hungary dropped its EPF veto.
digest.2026-06-10: 9 Jun: Trump said a 'very good deal' with Iran is in the final stretch, but Iran shot down a US Apache over Hormuz and he vowed a response. Brent fell ~4% to ~$91; gold closed at $4,286, the lowest since December; UST10 4.54%, Bund 10Y 3.05%; OAT-Bund jumped to 78bp (flagged); Hungary May CPI 1.8%; ~51% for an October Fed hike, ~70% for December.
digest.2026-06-11: 10 Jun: US strikes on Iranian air defences and Iranian retaliation on US bases; Trump: Iran 'will pay the price', more strikes coming. US May CPI 4.2% (core 2.9%, +0.2% m/m) was in line and a December Fed hike stays fully priced; the BoC held at 2.25%; Czech CPI 2.1% confirmed. Brent ~$93, TTF ~EUR50; UST10 4.53%, Bund 10Y 3.08% ahead of the ECB.
digest.2026-06-12: 11 Jun: the ECB hiked 25bp (DFR 2.25%, unanimous), raised its 2026 HICP forecast to 3.0% and stays meeting-by-meeting; the next hike is priced for September. Trump threatened 'very hard' strikes and seizing Kharg, then cancelled them and said a deal was reached; Brent -4.8% to ~$88.6, Wall Street +2%. US PPI +1.1% m/m; the CBRT held at 37%; UK Defence Secretary Healey resigned.
digest.2026-06-15: 12-14 Jun: MoU terms emerged (immediate Hormuz reopening, phased sanctions relief, a 60-day truce incl. Lebanon) amid Iranian denials; late Sunday Trump said a deal was reached, Hormuz open and the blockade lifted, signing 19 June. Brent ~$87 (-6% w/w), Bund 10Y <3%, gilt <4.8%; UK April GDP -0.1%; UMich 48.9; Romania May CPI 10.9%, Vestea named PM; a September ECB hike priced.
